_comment: Structural steel grades -- yield and tensile strength banded by thickness.
This file is REFERENCE DATA (ASET component 1). It is deliberately held as
a data file rather than in Python so that it can be checked, corrected and
signed off by an engineer who does not read code.
WHY THICKNESS BANDS, AND WHY THEY MATTER
The yield stress of hot-rolled steel falls as the section gets thicker,
because a thicker section cools more slowly and works less. So f_y is a
function of (grade, thickness), NOT of grade alone.
The consequence catches people out: a Grade 300 universal beam has a
DIFFERENT yield stress in its flange than in its web, because they are
different thicknesses. Any capacity expression that takes one f_y for the
whole section is wrong, usually by 5-15% and always in a direction that
depends on which thickness happened to be used.
AS 4100 handles this by using the flange f_y for flexure and the web f_y
for shear. This package therefore always asks for a thickness.
VERIFICATION: set status to VERIFIED and fill in checked_by/checked_on only
after every band has been confirmed against the printed standard. Until
then every number below is UNVERIFIED and must not be relied on for issue.
Confidence, worst first -- check in this order:
Plate grades   the band boundaries for AS/NZS 3678 plate are recalled
and the number of bands may be wrong.
Section grades AS/NZS 3679.1 hot-rolled sections. Three bands recalled
with reasonable confidence, but the boundaries (11 mm,
17 mm) must be confirmed.
SCHEMA
bands   [[max_thickness_mm, fy_MPa, fu_MPa], ...] ascending by thickness.
The LAST band applies to everything above the previous boundary,
and its max_thickness is the largest the grade is made in.
product what the grade is supplied as -- affects which standard governs

_note: AS 4100 Cl 1.4. Poisson's ratio of 0.25 is the value AS 4100 nominates,
which differs from the 0.3 used in much of the literature -- and G is
quoted directly rather than derived from E and nu, so the three are not
exactly consistent. Use the quoted G.
